messages:
Maria Chen: heads up — HF-to-Redwood conversion for the new chat model shows weird token counts in our eval set. tokenization differences seem to be the culprit. anyone seen this?
Samir Patel: saw similar with a Llama variant — whitespace + byte-fallback differences. can you paste an example?
Maria Chen: yeah. short repro: input `\"Hello\nWorld\"` tokenizes to 3 tokens on HF but 5 on our converted tokenizer. suspect unicode normalizer + byte fallback.
Kai Nguyen: is the HF tokenizer using `add_prefix_space` or a special normalizer (NFC/NFKC)? those change behaviour a lot for leading spaces/newlines.
Maria Chen: HF tokenizer config has: `add_prefix_space: true`, `normalizer: {type: "nfd"}` in one model, and another uses `nfkc`. messy. also `byte_fallback: true` in the tokenizer.json.
Taylor R: infra-bot ran the conversion tool yesterday — `rw-tokenizer-convert` — it defaults to enabling byte-fallback mode unless `--preserve-byte-fallback` set? infra-bot, can you confirm logs?
infra-bot: Converted tokenizer run: `rw-tokenizer-convert --src hf://some-model --dst /rw/tokenizers/some-model`
infra-bot: Detected hf config: `add_prefix_space=true`, `normalizer=none` (inferred), applied internal normalizer: `NFKC`.
Samir Patel: aha — converter inferred a normalizer when HF had a pipeline of pretokenizers+normalizers. that mismatch will split e.g. U+00A0 vs space and change byte fallback behavior.
Lucas M: concrete example from eval: input "Résumé" HF tokens: [`Res`, `umé`] ; converted tokenizer: [`Re`, `s`, `um`, `é`] — q8 model then produced shorter completions and rouge dropped 4 pts on the subset.
Maria Chen: thanks — that explains the quality regression. what's a minimal fix so we don't have to re-run full model onboarding?
Kai Nguyen: short-term: force the converter to copy HF normalizer and pretokenizer exactly. try `rw-tokenizer-convert --copy-normalizer --copy-pretokenizer` or export HF tokenizer to json and feed that. also ensure `add_prefix_space` matches.
Taylor R: also check special tokens mapping — we had a case where `<|system|>` became `<s>` and chat templates mismatched, causing shifted inputs. small seed mismatch can blow evals.
Samir Patel: proposed quick checklist: 1) export `tokenizer.json` from HF via `tokenizer.save_pretrained('.')` 2) run converter with `--preserve-normalizer --preserve-pretokenizer --preserve-byte-fallback` 3) assert `tokenizer.encode(sample)` equals HF for a few canonical samples (english, accent, NBSP, emojis).
Maria Chen: I ran that checklist. step 3 failed for NBSP (U+00A0) -> HF keeps as single white token but converted splits into `Ġ` + bytes. any idea?
Lucas M: NBSP is often normalized by NFKC -> space. If HF used no normalizer, and converter applied NFKC by default, that explains it. set `--normalizer none` in convert or explicitly pass HF normalizer config.
Samir Patel: added a tiny test harness: `samples = ["Hello\u00A0World", "Résumé", "\nstart", "emoji: \u{1F600}"]` then `for s in samples: assert hf_tok.encode(s)==rw_tok.encode(s)` — fails reveal which samples differ.
Maria Chen: perfect. I ran harness, found two mismatches: NBSP and leading newline. NBSP fix by forcing `normalizer: none`. Leading newline fixed by ensuring `add_prefix_space=true` on converted tokenizer.
Taylor R: record this in onboarding checklist. also run eval-bot to snapshot token counts and a short rouge check before and after changes.
eval-bot: Scheduled eval: small-qa-suite on `some-model` (q8 + rw-tokenizer fixed). job id 20260314-87.
Kai Nguyen: long-term we should make converter idempotent: if HF provides `tokenizer_config.json` or `tokenizer.json`, copy verbatim unless `--normalize` passed. also add a `--compat-check` that compares encoded outputs on a small corpus and fails early.
Maria Chen: agreed. I'll open a PR with the `--compat-check` harness and a docs note about special tokens and chat templates mapping.
Samir Patel: and add a warning in console when converter changes normalizer or byte fallback semantics. small UX win.
Maria Chen: thanks all — saved us from a subtle quality regression. I'll post the PR link once ready. :raised_hands:
Taylor R: nice catch. ping @security if any token mapping touches special tokens for prompts (we need to ensure canonicalization).
Lucas M: FYI, I pushed a small test file to the onboarding repo: `tests/tokenizer_compat_cases.txt` with NBSP, emojis, combining marks. use it in the converter CI.
Maria Chen: excellent — closing the loop.
